# Review consequential editorial patterns

Use the relevant example during a detailed edit. Start from the actual source and reader's purpose; a matching phrase alone does not establish a defect. These original examples do not add domain rules to a real project.

Material findings change a fact, condition, accepted meaning or authorised action. Contextual findings depend on the audience, document type and author voice. Review priority is an editorial judgement, not an automated score.

| Pattern | Concern | Review priority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [E001: Changed project meaning](#e001) | Consistency | Material |
| [E002: Lost condition](#e002) | Accuracy | Material |
| [E003: Invented result](#e003) | Evidence | Material |
| [E004: Evidence gap becomes a blanket stop](#e004) | Actionability | Material |
| [E005: Data structure becomes prose](#e005) | Readability | Contextual |
| [E006: Commentary hides the finding](#e006) | Navigation | Contextual |
| [E007: Necessary context is missing](#e007) | Accessibility | Contextual |
| [E008: Editing flattens the author's voice](#e008) | Voice | Contextual |

<a id="e001"></a>
## E001: Changed project meaning

**Review priority:** Material. **Concern:** Consistency.

**Invented source facts:** Reviewed means all document checks are complete. Approval is a separate decision that has not been made.

**Before**

> Your application is approved.

**After**

> All document checks are complete. An approval decision is still pending.

**Why this edit helps:** Restore the distinction between completed checks and approval rather than polishing the wrong state.

**When to keep a different form:** Keep an approved label when the governing source records an approval decision. Different audience labels are acceptable when their meanings agree.

**Related guidance:** [Geekist project-language review](https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/blob/main/standards/review.md).

<a id="e002"></a>
## E002: Lost condition

**Review priority:** Material. **Concern:** Accuracy.

**Invented source facts:** Only workspace owners can export selected notes. The supported format is Markdown.

**Before**

> Anyone can export all notes in any format.

**After**

> Workspace owners can export selected notes as Markdown.

**Why this edit helps:** Retain the actor, selection boundary and supported format that change what the reader may do.

**When to keep a different form:** A short label may omit detail when the adjacent explanation makes the relevant conditions clear. Do not remove a condition that changes a user's decision.

**Related guidance:** [Geekist project-language review](https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/blob/main/standards/review.md), [Humanizer v3.1.0](https://github.com/blader/humanizer/blob/0ef9fe5bc3572734fd3ae6c448fe00a30cd5dcf0/SKILL.md).

<a id="e003"></a>
## E003: Invented result

**Review priority:** Material. **Concern:** Evidence.

**Invented source facts:** Six internal participants gave feedback on the export flow. The trial did not measure time savings.

**Before**

> Our trial proved that export cuts reporting time in half.

**After**

> Six internal participants gave feedback on the export flow.

**Why this edit helps:** Describe the observed result and leave the unsupported time-saving claim out. Record the measurement needed if that stronger claim matters.

**When to keep a different form:** Retain a quantified benefit when a relevant measurement supports it, including the population and conditions needed to interpret the figure.

**Related guidance:** [Humanizer v3.1.0](https://github.com/blader/humanizer/blob/0ef9fe5bc3572734fd3ae6c448fe00a30cd5dcf0/SKILL.md), [Plain Language Editor](https://github.com/marketingskills/plain-language-editor/blob/df7b314509eb47a722aa620f11784fab76a595e6/SKILL.md).

<a id="e004"></a>
## E004: Evidence gap becomes a blanket stop

**Review priority:** Material. **Concern:** Actionability.

**Invented source facts:** A reversible local adapter prototype and local tests are authorised. Real-client behaviour has not been checked. No external deployment is authorised.

**Before**

> Compatibility is unproven, so stop all implementation.

**After**

> Build the authorised local prototype and run local tests. Check real-client behaviour before claiming compatibility. Keep external deployment outside this work.

**Why this edit helps:** Separate the missing compatibility evidence from the work already authorised and preserve the actual external-action boundary.

**When to keep a different form:** Keep a stop instruction when a demonstrated incompatibility, required input, permission boundary or explicit user instruction blocks that named action.

**Related guidance:** [Geekist project-language review](https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/blob/main/standards/review.md).

<a id="e005"></a>
## E005: Data structure becomes prose

**Review priority:** Contextual. **Concern:** Readability.

**Invented source facts:** An invited reviewer can view a report until 14 November. The reviewer cannot edit it.

**Before**

> The report object has a reviewer-scoped read-only access grant with a 14 November expiry attribute.

**After**

> The invited reviewer can view this report until 14 November, but cannot edit it.

**Why this edit helps:** Explain the actor, action and limit rather than making the reader reconstruct a permission record.

**When to keep a different form:** Keep exact field names and values in API or schema reference material. Explain their consequences alongside the contract instead of renaming identifiers.

**Related guidance:** [Plain Language Editor](https://github.com/marketingskills/plain-language-editor/blob/df7b314509eb47a722aa620f11784fab76a595e6/SKILL.md), [Geekist project-language review](https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/blob/main/standards/review.md).

<a id="e006"></a>
## E006: Commentary hides the finding

**Review priority:** Contextual. **Concern:** Navigation.

**Invented source facts:** The import stopped because the supplied file has no header row. The user must add the row before retrying.

**Before**

> It is important to note the following key finding: the import failed due to an issue with the header.

**After**

> The import stopped because the file has no header row. Add the header row and retry.

**Why this edit helps:** Lead with the observed failure and useful next action, replacing vague commentary with the actual cause.

**When to keep a different form:** Keep navigation instructions when they help the reader use a long guide or choose a relevant section. Not every sentence about the document is redundant.

**Related guidance:** [Plain Language Editor](https://github.com/marketingskills/plain-language-editor/blob/df7b314509eb47a722aa620f11784fab76a595e6/SKILL.md), [Humanizer v3.1.0](https://github.com/blader/humanizer/blob/0ef9fe5bc3572734fd3ae6c448fe00a30cd5dcf0/SKILL.md).

<a id="e007"></a>
## E007: Necessary context is missing

**Review priority:** Contextual. **Concern:** Accessibility.

**Invented source facts:** A queue for each project keeps its scheduling separate. The intended audience includes readers unfamiliar with queues.

**Before**

> The per-project queue resolves the scheduling issue.

**After**

> Each project has its own waiting list of jobs, called a queue, so its scheduling stays separate from other projects.

**Why this edit helps:** Introduce the necessary term and explain the consequence without promising an unmeasured performance improvement.

**When to keep a different form:** Use the accepted specialist term directly when the intended reader already knows it or can reach its definition. Do not expand every familiar abbreviation on every page.

**Related guidance:** [Geekist project-language review](https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/blob/main/standards/review.md), [Plain Language Editor](https://github.com/marketingskills/plain-language-editor/blob/df7b314509eb47a722aa620f11784fab76a595e6/SKILL.md).

<a id="e008"></a>
## E008: Editing flattens the author's voice

**Review priority:** Contextual. **Concern:** Voice.

**Invented source facts:** The author is writing a lightly witty personal essay about repeatedly losing draft notes. No product performance claim is being made.

**Before**

> The author experienced repeated difficulties with draft-note retention.

**After**

> I kept losing my draft notes. Apparently, I was running a disappearing-ink experiment.

**Why this edit helps:** Use the author's stated register while preserving the event. The second sentence is an obvious humorous aside, not a technical claim.

**When to keep a different form:** Keep neutral wording in a technical reference or when humour would obscure a consequential condition. Preserve uncertainty and personal detail when they carry meaning.

**Related guidance:** [Humanizer v3.1.0](https://github.com/blader/humanizer/blob/0ef9fe5bc3572734fd3ae6c448fe00a30cd5dcf0/SKILL.md), [Geekist project-language review](https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/blob/main/standards/review.md).

## Sources and local adaptation

The examples and explanations in this reference are original local writing. Stable identifiers and explicit exceptions make findings easier to inspect and discuss. No external pattern catalogue or revision template is copied.

- [Geekist project-language review](https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/blob/main/standards/review.md): Project meanings, source constraints and bounded next actions govern each revision.
- [Humanizer v3.1.0](https://github.com/blader/humanizer/blob/0ef9fe5bc3572734fd3ae6c448fe00a30cd5dcf0/SKILL.md): Concrete editing examples, factual checks and contextual exceptions inform the presentation.
- [Plain Language Editor](https://github.com/marketingskills/plain-language-editor/blob/df7b314509eb47a722aa620f11784fab76a595e6/SKILL.md): Stable pattern identifiers and checks for meaning, claims and sentence relationships inform the organisation. No upstream catalogue is copied.

This reference supports source-based editing. It does not detect AI authorship, verify claims automatically or require every example to be loaded for a small change.
